name: Non-syndromic Renal or Urinary Tract Malformation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Consensus Criteria for Non-syndromic Renal or Urinary Tract Malformations

criteria.description: Presence of congenital structural anomaly of the kidney or urinary tract confirmed by imaging
No clinical or genetic evidence of syndromic involvement or extrarenal malformations
Positive family history of isolated renal or urinary tract malformations
Normal neurodevelopmental and systemic examination excluding syndromic diagnosis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital renal or urinary tract structural anomaly on imaging with exclusion of syndromic features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may be used to exclude syndromic causes but is not mandatory for diagnosis.

pathognomonic.notes: Detected on prenatal or postnatal imaging
searchTerms: kidney growth problem present at birth

pathognomonic.notes: Due to urinary tract obstruction or reflux
searchTerms: swelling of one or both kidneys
enlarged kidney due to urine backup
bladder urine reflux without other issues

common.notes: Often secondary to urinary tract malformation

common.symptomName: Impaired renal function or elevated serum creatinine
common.notes: May develop over time depending on severity

common.symptomName: Abdominal or flank mass detected on examination
common.notes: Palpable enlarged kidney or cystic mass
May develop in older children or adults
searchTerms: high blood pressure from kidney problem
raised blood pressure due to kidney issue

occasional.notes: May be associated with urinary tract dysfunction

occasional.symptomName: Growth retardation secondary to chronic kidney disease
searchTerms: growth delay due to chronic kidney disease
poor growth related to kidney problems

rare.notes: Due to structural anomalies affecting bladder function
searchTerms: leaking urine not caused by infection

rare.notes: Rare complication of chronic kidney disease

laboratory: Elevated serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen in advanced cases
Urinalysis showing microscopic hematuria and proteinuria
Urine culture positive in recurrent urinary tract infections
imaging: Ultrasound showing renal hypoplasia, dysplasia, or hydronephrosis
Magnetic resonance urography for detailed urinary tract anatomy
genetic: Exclusion of syndromic genetic mutations (e.g., PAX2, HNF1B) to confirm non-syndromic status
Family history suggestive of autosomal dominant inheritance in some cases
other: Normal neurodevelopmental assessment excluding syndromic involvement
Blood pressure monitoring for secondary hypertension

distinguishingFeatures: Genetic mutations associated with syndromic forms
Characteristic imaging findings of obstruction without reflux

redFlags: Hypertension in a child with known renal anomaly
references: Orphanet: Non-syndromic renal or urinary tract malformation, ORPHA:93546
